summary: On an Earth level, a blessed pickaxe can call dig.c:mkcavearea(FALSE) after the hero finishes cutting rock. JavaScript records the omitted helper call and ends the occupation, while C expands the cave, updates vision, blocks on the message, and then finishes. This is a bounded caller repair in dig.c:dig plus whole implementations of its missing static helpers; it grants no whole-dig credit.

source.branch: In dig.c:dig, after effort exceeds 100 while the current Earth-level target is STONE or SCORR, C tests the blessed pick with rn2(3). On success it calls mkcavearea(FALSE) and jumps to cleanup. JS dig.js has the same branch and draw but calls note_unported('dig.c mkcavearea'), finishes the occupation, and returns before the source terrain, vision, message-wait, and cleanup behavior. The two preceding screens match; the first difference is at zero-based step 333.
callers: C apply.c:doapply -> dig.c:use_pick_axe/use_pick_axe2 installs dig as the occupation; allmain.c later invokes dig.c:dig. JavaScript apply.js dispatches through js/dig.js:use_pick_axe/use_pick_axe2, and allmain.js invokes the same exported dig callback.

C dig.c:dig calls mkcavearea(FALSE) for blessed Earth digging and mkcavearea(TRUE) for the cursed or ordinary Earth roll. mkcavearea calls rm_waslit and mkcavepos; mkcavepos changes map/vision state and calls feel_newsym.

The selected recording reaches the blessed FALSE arm. Existing source history records mkcavearea as an unported gap; an earlier dig goal explicitly parked Earth-level mkcavearea evidence as unavailable before this source-reaching v53 recording. This task does not close the incomplete whole dig source unit.
dependencies: rm_waslit is a pure source helper whose result is consumed by mkcavearea; implement it and pin its C neighborhood predicate in a focused test.

mkcavepos and mkcavearea are currently absent from js/dig.js. Implement both complete static functions and reuse the existing terrain, message, vision, monster-location, and display operations at the matching C call sites. The mkcavearea rockit=true branch also uses the C monster relocation and crash-message path; do not infer runtime coverage of that arm from this blessed case.
Do not edit dig.c:dighole or its JS magical-trap caller: that exact source function is reserved by A and is outside this task.
